did_you_know.text: In the Bible the phrase 'The LORD spoke to Moses' signals that important divine instructions follow.
The name 'Canaan' refers both to the land and to the people (the Canaanites) who lived in the ancient Levant.
In biblical Hebrew 'Negev' denotes the southern, arid part of the land; the word is connected to 'south' and dryness.
Kadesh‑Barnea mentioned here also appears in the wilderness narratives and serves as an important southern landmark.
The references to 'Egypt' in the borders underline that Canaan lay next to Egyptian spheres of influence at various times.
The 'Great Sea' in the Bible typically refers to the Mediterranean Sea — the western border of Canaan.
Describing northern borders with mountains shows that in antiquity mountains were used as clear natural boundary markers.
Place names like 'Hazar Enan' or 'Shfama' are hard to pinpoint on modern maps, so scholars disagree about their exact locations.
The 'Salt Sea' here is the present‑day Dead Sea — the lowest land point on Earth.
Division 'by lot' (goral) was a common biblical method: casting lots was used to assign land among the tribes.
